blocks.text: LINGAYEN, Pangasinan — Heavy rains in August and September, brought by the long habagat rains (Southeast monsoon) and tropical cyclones, helped replenish Pangasinan’s water reserves, giving the province a buffer as it braces for the dry months and worsening El Niño. The rainfall filled the San Roque Multipurpose Project reservoirs and recharged underground water sources, giving farmers a water supply for the second rice cropping season and cultivation of vegetables and corn, according to Pangasinan Provincial Agriculture Officer Dalisay Moya. “The replenished groundwater is also expected to benefit farmers who depend on wells and other underground sources to irrigate their fields.
